history.period: 8th century CE (c. 756-773 CE, during Krishna I's reign; some elements completed later)
history.summary: The Kailasa Temple (Cave 16) at Ellora is the largest of the rock-cut Hindu temples at the Ellora Caves and the world's largest monolithic rock-cut structure, carved entirely from a single basalt cliff. Most of its excavation is attributed to the 8th-century Rashtrakuta king Krishna I (r. c. 756-773), taking around 18 years (verify) with thousands of workers, who removed an estimated 200,000 to 400,000 tonnes of rock using a unique top-down excavation technique: three trenches were cut into the cliff to isolate the rock mass, then the temple was carved downward from the top, so the entire design had to be visualized in advance. Dedicated to Lord Shiva as Kailasanatha, the temple is conceived as Mount Kailash, Shiva's celestial abode; its multi-storeyed Dravidian structure, 32.6 m high, shows traces of Pallava and Chalukya styles, with a gopuram, courtyard, Nandi pavilion, and relief panels depicting the Ramayana, Mahabharata, and Vishnu's avatars. Legend credits architect Kokasa (verify), and tradition says the temple was once coated in white plaster to resemble snow-covered Kailash (verify). One account says Aurangzeb sent men to destroy it in 1682 and they gave up after three years (verify). IMPORTANT FOR THE DATASET: it is a UNESCO World Heritage monument (Ellora Caves, 1983) and an ASI-protected archaeological site; regular worship is not held inside and it functions primarily as a tourist/heritage monument - the dataset owner should decide whether to keep it.

name: Kailasa Temple
town_description: Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar (formerly Aurangabad) is a historic city in the Marathwada region of Maharashtra, founded by the Mughals and long known as the 'City of Gates'. It is the gateway to two UNESCO World Heritage cave complexes - Ajanta (about 100 km) and Ellora (about 30 km), the latter housing the Kailasa Temple at Ellora village. The city's landmarks include Bibi Ka Maqbara (the 'Mini Taj'), Daulatabad (Devagiri) Fort, and the Grishneshwar Jyotirlinga near Ellora.

travel.airport: Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar Airport (formerly Aurangabad Airport), approx. 30 km from Ellora; taxis and app cabs available.
travel.railway: Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar (Aurangabad) railway station, approx. 30 km; Jalgaon station is an alternative (verify). Autos, buses and taxis run from the city.
travel.road: The temple stands at Ellora village, about 30 km northwest of Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar city on the Ellora Cave Road; MSRTC buses and autos run from the city's central bus stop. An on-site shuttle bus (approx. Rs. 22) links the Buddhist, Hindu and Jain cave clusters along the 2 km complex.

visitor_information.best_time: October to February for cool, pleasant weather (15-25°C); early morning 6-9 AM to beat crowds and heat. Maha Shivaratri (February-March) is the most spiritually charged time but crowded.
visitor_information.opening_hours: 6:00 AM to 6:00 PM daily; closed on Tuesdays (verify - one source lists 9:00 AM to 5:30 PM). Last entry approx. 5:00-5:30 PM. Entry fee: Rs. 40 for Indian/SAARC visitors, Rs. 600 for foreign nationals, free for children under 15; video camera fee approx. Rs. 25 extra (verify current fees on the ASI portal). No flash photography where posted; hire an ASI-authorized guide for the carvings.
